risk_if_not_implemented: Without Input Data Validation, applications may be built and deployed with exploitable design and coding weaknesses that adversaries can leverage. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Modification / Loss of System Integrity (R-AM-2), System / Data Compromise (Technical Vector) (R-BC-4), System / Service Compromise (R-EX-7), Loss of Data Integrity (R-IP-3), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Human Error (MT-9), Data Quality Degradation / Data Poisoning (MT-12).

compensating_control_1.name: Secure Baseline Configurations
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to develop, document and maintain secure baseline configurations for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that are consistent with industry-accepted hardening standards.
compensating_control_1.justification: Secure Baseline Configurations (CFG-04) provides configuration hardening that compensates for the absence of Input Data Validation (TDA-12) by eliminating unnecessary services and enforcing secure settings to reduce inherent exposure. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Secure Software Development Practices (SSDP)
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to develop applications based on Secure Software Development Practices (SSDP).
compensating_control_2.justification: Secure Software Development Practices (SSDP) (TDA-05) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Input Data Validation (TDA-12) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Technology applicability. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
